1                                       INTRODUCTION

2    Q.   Please state your name and business address.

3    A.   My name is Elizabeth Acosta. My business address is the New Mexico Public Regulation

4         Commission (“Commission” or “NMPRC”), P.O. Box 1269, Santa Fe, NM 87504.

5

6    Q.   What is your position with the Commission?

7    A.   I am employed as a Public Utilities Economist with the Utility Division of the NMPRC

8         Staff (“Staff”).

9

10   Q.   Please describe your educational background and professional experience.

11   A.   I received a Bachelor of Science in Finance with a Financial Management emphasis and a

12        Minor in Marketing in 2014 from Arkansas State University. I also hold a Master of Arts

13        in Economics with a concentration in Public Utility Policy and Regulation from New

14        Mexico State University, received in December 2024. I was employed at El Paso Water

15        from 2019 to 2025, working in various capacities, most recently as a Business & Customer

16        Service Manager. In February 2025, I joined the NMPRC’s Utility Division as a Public

17        Utilities Economist in the Economics Bureau.

18

19   Q.   Have you previously testified before this Commission?

20   A.   Yes. Please see attached Exhibit EA-1 for a summary of cases in which I have provided

21        testimony.

22

                                                 1
                                                CASE NO. 25-00082-UT
                                          PREPARED DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                                ELIZABETH ACOSTA

1    Q.      What is the purpose of your testimony in this case?

2    A.      The purpose of my testimony is to provide a review of El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE”

3            or the “Company”) Application requesting approval to revise retail rates and other

4            associated relief (“Application”), specifically focusing on EPE’s request for approval to

5            make revisions to Rate No. 15 – Miscellaneous Service Charges, and the Company’s

6            proposed changes to its monthly Residential Customer Charge. Additionally, I will be

7            providing a review of EPE’s compliance with certain requests set forth in the

8            Recommended Decision, as adopted in relevant part by the Commission’s Order Adopting

9            Recommended Decision with Modifications in Case No. 20-00104-UT1.

10

11   Q.      What are Staff’s recommendations in this case, as addressed in your testimony?

12   A.      As addressed in my testimony, Staff recommends approval of EPE’s proposed revisions to

13           the Miscellaneous Service Charges. Approval of the revisions is in the public interest as it

14           aligns the charges with the costs of providing such services to those customers that require

15           the services. The changes proposed by the Company will result in a net reduction of

16           $241,000 in total miscellaneous revenues.

17

18           Additionally, Staff recommends approval of a $12.00 monthly Residential Customer

19           Charge, as proposed by Staff. Staff’s recommendation is in the public interest as it supports

2                                     RESIDENTIAL CUSTOMER CHARGE

3    Q.         What Residential Customer Charge is EPE proposing in its Application?

4    A.         EPE is proposing a fixed monthly Residential Customer Charge of $19.17, a $12.17 or

5               174% increase over its current residential customer charge of $7.00. The Company is also

6               proposing a phase-in of this proposed increase – Phase 1 would reflect an increase to

7               $14.56, and Phase 2 would demonstrate the final increase to the proposed $19.17. Based

8               on the Company’s cost of service, without the requested increase to the customer charge,

9               the Company will only recover 38.6% of customer-related costs through the customer

10              charge.3

11

12              It is also important to note that in EPE’s last rate case, Case No. 20-00104-UT, the

13              Commission issued a Final Order, retaining the $7.00 charge and rejecting the $9.00

14              customer charge set forth in the Recommended Decision. An increase to the Company’s

15              residential customer charge has not been made since EPE’s 2009 rate case, where parties

16              ultimately stipulated to the current $7.00 charge, which the Commission has maintained

17              through subsequent rate cases.

18

19   Q.         How does EPE’s proposed monthly customer charge for the Residential customer

20              class compare to other IOUs in New Mexico?




     3
         See Amended Direct Testimony of Manuel Carrasco at page 41, lines 17-19.

                                                              4
                                               CASE NO. 25-00082-UT
                                         PREPARED DIRECT TESTIMONY OF

1    A.      EPE’s proposed monthly residential customer charge of $19.17 is higher than both

2            Southwestern Public Service Company’s (“SPS”) and Public Service Company of New

3            Mexico’s (“PNM”) current Commission approved residential fixed customer charges.

4            PNM’s current customer charge of $11.93 was a result of a stipulation in Case No. 24-

5            00089-UT4. In its pending rate case, Case No. 25-00079-UT5, SPS is proposing a monthly

6            customer charge of $15.50 in its proposed comprehensive stipulation, a 38.4% increase on

7            its current monthly charge of $11.20, however a revised charge has not been finalized in

8            that proceeding. Since each of the electric utilities referenced has a unique revenue

9            requirement that is utilized in determining its rates, the comparison provided is for

10           informational purposes only and should not be used as the sole justification for approving

11           or denying EPE’s proposed monthly charge.

12

13   Q.      Does Staff support EPE’s proposed increase to its monthly residential customer

14           charge?

15   A.      No. Staff supports an increase in EPE’s residential customer charge to move the charge

16           closer to the actual cost of service, which reduces intra-class subsidization and sends better

17           price signals to customers. This shift will provide more revenue stability for the Company

18           and help mitigate the fixed monthly costs the utility would incur regardless of the usage

19           levels of its customers.



     4
       See Case No. 24-00089-UT, In the Matter of the Application of Public Service Company of New Mexico for Revision
     of its Retail Electric Rates Pursuant to Advice Notice No. 625.
     5
       See Case No. 25-00079-UT, In the Matter of Southwestern Public Service Company’s Application for: (1) Revision
     of its Retail Rates Under Advice Notice 341; And (2) Other Associated Relief.

                                                            5
                                        CASE NO. 25-00082-UT
                                  PREPARED DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                        ELIZABETH ACOSTA

1

2         However, Staff has historically advocated for gradual increases to fixed monthly charges,

3         especially for residential customers. Increases in fixed monthly charges have a greater

4         impact on low usage customers compared to those customers with higher usage levels.

5         Therefore, higher fixed charges do not encourage conservation as greatly, as they limit

6         customers’ control over their bills. Additionally, large increases in the fixed monthly

7         customer charge for a residential customer have a more significant impact proportionally

8         than increases in the fixed customer charge for a large customer that uses more power.

9

10        For these reasons, Staff does not support EPE’s proposed residential customer charge of

11        $19.17. In Staff’s opinion, a 174% increase in the charge is excessive, goes against the

12        Commission’s long-standing policy of gradualism and could potentially result in rate

13        shock.

14

15   Q.   Is EPE making any other recommendations in its Application that will have a direct

16        impact on the proposed Residential customer charge?

17   A.   Yes. EPE is also recommending a Low-Income Rider that will provide a credit equal to the

18        monthly residential customer charge to customers who qualify, effectively zeroing out the

19        impact of the proposed customer charge on a qualifying customer’s monthly bill. A more

20        detailed discussion as well as Staff’s recommendations regarding the Low-Income Rider

21        is provided in the Direct Testimony of Richard J. Bunch on behalf of NMPRC Utility

22        Division Staff.

2    Q.   What is Staff’s recommended monthly customer charge for residential customers?

3    A.   Staff recommends a monthly residential customer charge of $12.00, which represents an

4         increase of $5.00 or 71%. Staff recommends a phase in of this increase – the Phase 1

5         residential customer charge is recommended to be $9.50 and the final recommended

6         monthly charge of $12.00 would be implemented in Phase 2. This more moderate increase

7         will provide residential customers with a smoother transition to new rates. Staff’s

8         recommendation provides reasonable movement towards fully recovering customer

9         component costs through the customer charge and reduces intra-class subsidies while

10        remaining consistent with the Commission’s long-standing policy of gradualism. Staff’s

11        rate design calculations are presented in the Direct Testimony of Douglas Jester on behalf

12        of NMPRC Utility Division Staff.


13                          MISCELLANEOUS SERVICE CHARGES

15        proposed by EPE in its Application.

16   A.   The various charges within Rate No. 15 – Miscellaneous Service Charges have been

17        updated by EPE to reflect the cost of providing the associated services. Staff is generally

18        supportive of the methodology used by the Company in calculating the rates for recovery

19        of the cost of service associated with each charge. Of the 31 currently active charges in its

20        New Mexico jurisdiction, eight received a significant reduction, all greater than 20%, while

6    Q.         Is EPE proposing to remove any miscellaneous service charges?

7    A.         Yes. EPE is proposing to remove two miscellaneous service charges from Rate No. 15:

8               Non-Pay Reconnect Charge at Pole (up to 200 amps or single-phase) and Non-Pay

9               Reconnect Charge at Pole (over 200 amps or three-phase). EPE operations personnel have

12              not the meter. As such, the charge has been renamed to Non-Pay Reconnect Charge at Pole

13              to remove any language referencing the amperage and AC power phases.7

20              a significant increase showing activity during the test year. The total individual charge

7    Q.        What does Staff recommend regarding EPE’s proposed changes to its Miscellaneous

8              Service Charges?

9    A.        Staff recommends approval of EPE’s proposed changes to Rate No. 15 - Miscellaneous

10             Service Charges. As discussed above, the Company’s proposed Miscellaneous Service

11             Charges were developed from a cost-causation perspective, and it is not in the public

12             interest for any of these charges to be set below the cost to provide the associated service.

13             These charges are not relevant to the majority of EPE’s customers, and therefore the full

14             cost of these services should be borne by the customers that cause the Company to incur

15             them.

10              Staff’s rate design recommendations are addressed by Douglas Jester.

12                                CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

13   Q.         Please summarize Staff’s conclusions and recommendations.

14   A.         As addressed in my testimony, Staff recommends approval of the proposed revisions to the

15              Miscellaneous Service Charges. Approval of the revisions is in the public interest as it

16              aligns the charges with the costs of providing such services to those customers that require

17              the services. The changes proposed by the Company will result in a net reduction of

18              $241,000 in total miscellaneous revenues.

19
